title: Phase-controlled recoverable entanglement in accelerated detector registers
abstract: We study recoverable entanglement in a four-qubit cluster-state register whose two detector qubits couple to a scalar field. A local preparation phase leaves the initial reference--register entanglement and detector marginal unchanged, but controls protection under collective noise. At the optimal phase, a fixed decoder recovers a Bell pair after any channel preserving the singlet and triplet sectors. For uniformly accelerated detectors at finite separation, an exact trace-norm formula shows that the same phase is optimal at every time within the secular weak-coupling dynamics. Small separation produces a slow decay, whose rate and phase-dependent amplitude we derive. Matching the local response to an inertial thermal bath gives an analytic optimum time for the entanglement contrast. A detector measurement and conditional phase correction recover a two-qubit teleportation resource. Spatial smearing and an ordered weak-coupling then small-separation limit specify the microscopic scope of the lifetime prediction.
summary: This paper investigates how entanglement stored in a multi-qubit register can be protected and recovered when the qubits interact with a noisy quantum field. By controlling the initial preparation phase, the authors show that the entanglement can be robustly recovered into a usable quantum resource like a Bell pair. The theoretical framework uses advanced tools from open quantum systems to analyze decay rates under various physical separation limits.
main_problem: The study focuses on quantifying and understanding the persistence and recovery of entanglement in a multi-qubit register coupled to an external quantum field.
main_result: The authors determine an optimal phase control that allows a fixed decoder to recover a Bell pair, and derive analytic formulas for the decay rate of this recoverable entanglement under various physical limits.
method: The analysis employs quantum channel theory, sector decomposition (singlet/triplet), and time evolution governed by Lindblad master equations, supplemented by weak-coupling and perturbation theory.
model_or_system: The system is a four-qubit cluster-state register whose two detector qubits interact with a massless scalar field. The dynamics are modeled using GKSL generators and analyzed in the context of quantum dissipative systems.
key_observables: Negativity ($N(ho)$), initial reference-register entanglement, and the fidelity of recovered quantum resources (e.g., Bell pairs, teleportation resources).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on the secular approximation, weak-coupling limits, and specific commutation relations between the noise channel and the system's symmetry sectors.

paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the phase-controlled recovery of entanglement in the general case, to deriving the time evolution of the negativity for accelerated detectors, and finally analyzing the limits imposed by finite separation and microscopic details using ordered limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for quantifying how quantum correlations (entanglement) can be protected and retrieved from noisy environments, which is central to quantum communication and quantum memory research.
